Vivek Ramaswamy looks on during AmericaFest, in Phoenix, Arizona, US, on December 19, 2025 File: Cheney Orr/Reuters]By Elizabeth MelimopoulosPublished On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026
An attack advertisement by Republican Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy targeting his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton, has sparked criticism within his own party, less than two weeks before November 3 midterm elections in the United States.
The ad features Acton’s estranged mother accusing Acton of being a liar.
Recommended Stories list of 1 itemlist 1 of 1Trump backs Ramaswamy ad featuring rival Amy Acton’s estranged motherend of list
Ramaswamy has refused to withdraw the ad, even as senior Republicans have called for its removal.
So what does the ad show, why has it sparked controversy and could it affect Ohio’s governor’s race?
Here is what we know:
What does Vivek Ramaswamy’s advert show?
The ad, which began circulating online on Monday, features Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, accusing her daughter of lying about her childhood and suggesting she has a mental illness.
“It’s not easy for a mother to say this, but Amy has a serious problem. She is a liar. She lies about her past,” Arthur said in the video.
Arthur also disputed Acton’s account of experiencing homelessness and living in a tent as a child as she urged Ohioans not to vote for her daughter.Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, second from left [File: Carolyn Kaster/AP]
However, the ad does not mention that the two have been estranged since 1978 when Acton was 12 and was removed from her mother’s custody after her stepfather was charged with raping her.

How Netanyahu reshaped Israel after 18 years in powerBy Nour OdehPublished On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026
To his supporters, he is known as “King Bibi”; but to his opponents, he is the king of security failures and corruption.
Disputes over names aside, what is not in question is that Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, has left his mark on the country’s institutions, politics and social attitudes during a decades-long career that has been defined by Israel’s lurch to the right.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3The kingmakers who could determine Israel’s electionlist 2 of 3Hegseth meets Netanyahu on unannounced Israel visitlist 3 of 3Trump backs Netanyahu: Is the US planning a new Iran attack with Israel?end of list
As he seeks re-election in Israel’s October 27 polls, analysts say his most enduring domestic legacy may be the right-wing, militaristic opposition that he has helped create and now faces.
Born in 1949, Netanyahu entered Israel’s central political stage in the early 1990s by fuelling anger at possible peace deals with the Palestinians and Syria.
Israeli political leaders have accused him of leading incitement that motivated the 1995 assassination of then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, who was leading negotiations with the Palestine Liberation Organization, by an ultranationalist Israeli. Netanyahu had led rallies in which participants depicted Rabin in a Nazi SS uniform and held signs of him in the crosshairs of a gun, while others shouted “traitor”.

Signs of battles between Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthis west of Taiz on Wednesday [AFP]By AbdulHakim HelalPublished On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026
Taiz, Yemen – It was approaching 10:30am in the dialysis centre of the Republican Hospital in Taiz when a machine began filtering excess fluids, toxins and salts from the blood of Omar Mukhtar Hammoud.
The 16-year-old suffers from kidney failure and is one of 270 patients who regularly receive dialysis at the centre in the government-held city in southwest Yemen. But with essential medical supplies and fuel running critically low under the renewed Houthi siege, doctors fear they may soon be unable to provide the treatment that keeps their patients alive.

Dr Essam Mahyoub Dahan, the centre’s director, warned that a complete shutdown could happen within days.
“Because of the siege and the shortage of diesel and medical solutions, we have recently been forced to reduce dialysis sessions from four hours to just two and a half,” Dahan told Al Jazeera. “We know this is not adequate, but we have no choice if we are to keep the centre operating for as long as possible before it shuts down completely.”
Dahan said the centre’s remaining stocks of specialised dialysis solutions were also close to running out.

A child stands next to the rubble of a building damaged in an Israeli attack on Qennarit, in southern Lebanon, on June 20, 2026 [Reuters]By Justin SalhaniPublished On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026
Beirut, Lebanon – As Israel’s October 27 election nears, so does the possibility that the government that has overseen the invasion and reoccupation of southern Lebanon could be deposed.
But for people in Lebanon, optimism that a change in the Israeli government will bode well for Israel’s neighbours is low.
“I don’t think anything major – or at all – will change for Lebanon even if there’s a change in [Israeli] leadership,” said Beirut resident Fouad Debs.
“Any internal change might lead to small, insignificant changes just to show the outside world that Israeli society and politics are not messed up or evil,” added the lawyer.
For many in Lebanon, Israel’s history of airspace violations, ground invasions and occupation has led to a general atmosphere of distrust, regardless of who is in charge of the country.
“Proof is what people [in Israel] are saying as the elections [approach],” said Karim Safieddine, a Beirut-based nonresident fellow at the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy.
“No one is promising withdrawal, and no one is addressing south Lebanon as a crisis or a mistake,” he added, noting that the “general Israeli establishment looks at Lebanon as its prize”.
Israel and the Lebanese Shia group Hezbollah have been fighting, with different levels of intensity, since October 2023 in the wake of the Hamas-led attack in southern Israel and Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip that followed it. Israel imposes full closure of occupied West Bank after Hebron shooting kills two soldiersBy Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026
Israeli forces have raided towns, detaining dozens of Palestinians, hours after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced ordering a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank following an attack in the city of Hebron that killed two Israeli soldiers.
Israeli forces raided at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank, detaining dozens of Palestinians, Al Jazeera correspondents reported on Saturday.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Israel preparing full lockdown of occupied West Bank after Hebron gunfightlist 2 of 3Israeli roadblocks disrupt schools and medical care in West Bank villagelist 3 of 3Israel locks down occupied West Bank after Hebron shootingend of list
The military raids targeted several northern cities and towns, including Nablus, Jenin, Tubas and Qalqilya.
In Nablus, Israeli forces carried out arrests and raided Palestinian homes in the villages of Jalud and Qaryut. Arrests were also reported in Arrabeh and Burqin, near Jenin, while Israeli forces entered Tubas and the nearby town of Aqqaba.
In the southern occupied West Bank, Israeli bulldozers demolished a three-storey building in Hebron, with families given five minutes to collect their belongings. Israeli forces also ordered hundreds of Palestinian families to forcibly evacuate their homes in the Ein Deir Bahha area of Hebron and its surroundings.
Israeli troops also surrounded the home of one of the suspects in the shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers in Hebron, while carrying out raids in the city’s al-Jalda neighbourhood.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth speaks at a roundtable event in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC [File: Alex Brandon/AP]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and ReutersPublished On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026
The United States Department of Defense has designated Confucius Institutes, Chinese-funded cultural centres on university campuses, as a threat to US national security.
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the move on Friday in a video posted on social media, saying the Pentagon added the organisations to its list of institutions that threaten national security.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3No ‘turmoil’ at the White Houselist 2 of 3US-Ukraine relations sour as Trump, Zelenskyy clash over talks, armslist 3 of 3Hegseth meets Netanyahu on unannounced Israel visitend of list
Washington has long accused the centres of serving as Chinese propaganda tools and has taken steps to crack down on them.
Hegseth said Confucius Institutes had operated in disguise after being restricted by Congress, calling them “sleeper organisations”.
“It turns out that 80 new propaganda cells across 30 universities had popped up using different names and different charters, but with the same mission: to steal intellectual property and to infiltrate the minds of American students,” he said.
In the video, Hegseth said that Chinese government-backed cultural programmes had infiltrated universities and reappeared in new guises despite congressional restrictions.
Over the past two months, the Pentagon has “systematically dismantled every single one of these organisations”, he said.
The Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment.
